svg.aria-label: The map of the code. On the player's Windows PC the launcher (Tk, opendmt3/client: its pages, actions.py, hosting.py, remote.py, updates.py) only reads the client data, makes openDMT3's own folder from it at PLAY (core/cabinet/steps.py: the client copy, the card reader library with the in-game overlay, the settings, the card), and starts the game from there, with the card reader library of native/cardreader in it. Playing on this PC, the launcher runs the server inside itself; on another server, it signs in over the HTTP API for the player's card and records. The game logs in by card and sends its results over the game's own protocol. The server (opendmt3/server, with Docker or Python) is one process: the site and its API on port 4730 (Starlette, web/), the game server on port 4725 (asyncio, connection.py and messages.py), their services (services/) and one SQLite file (db/). Both parts share opendmt3/core
